PhD Programs Application Requirements (In Person)
The application is now available for doctoral programs! Apply now for fall 2027 admission.
Start Your Application →
School of Arts, Humanities and Culture
Programs: Near Eastern and Judaic Studies
Expand All
Application Requirements
Application Fee
The online application fee is $75. This fee is required for all applicants unless you are eligible for an application fee waiver.
Transcripts
You must hold (or be about to earn) a bachelor’s degree from an accredited U.S. or international institution. Three-year international degrees equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's degree are also accepted. Unofficial transcripts are accepted for application review. Official transcripts are only required upon enrollment.
You should provide transcripts for institutions where:
You earned (or will earn) a degree.
You completed 12 or more credits that do not appear as graded courses on another transcript you are uploading.
Note: If you attended more than 4 schools, only list the 4 most relevant (e.g., your Bachelor’s and Master’s institutions).
Letters of Recommendation
Near Eastern and Judaic Studies: Three letters of recommendation are required
Academic references (professors, or research/thesis advisors) are strongly preferred. Select a person who can speak to your abilities as a student, research potential, and preparedness for graduate study. You are welcome to submit a professional reference, especially if you do not have a recent academic contact. Select someone who can speak in detail about your skills and approach to work.
Résumé
A current résumé detailing educational and employment history is required. Candidates with little or no full-time work experience should include internships and/or part-time work.
GRE (Optional)
Submission of GRE scores is entirely optional. If you choose to submit scores, you may submit unofficial scores at the time of application. If you submitted unofficial scores as part of your application, are offered admission and choose to enroll, you must submit official score reports and send them directly to Brandeis Graduate Admissions from the testing agency.
GRE scores are valid for five (5) years from the original test date-Scores must be valid at the time your application is submitted. The GRE code is 3092.

To view your program’s specific question(s) and word count recommendations, please begin your online application and view the Statement of Purpose instructions.

To view your program’s specific writing sample instructions, please log into the online application.

Programs: Biochemistry and Biophysics, Chemistry, Computer Science, Mathematics, Molecular and Cell Biology, Neuroscience, Physics, Psychology

Application Requirements
Application Fee
The online application fee is $75. This fee is required for all applicants unless you are eligible for an application fee waiver.
Transcripts
You must hold (or be about to earn) a bachelor’s degree from an accredited U.S. or international institution. Three-year international degrees equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's degree are also accepted. Unofficial transcripts are accepted for application review. Official transcripts are only required upon enrollment.
You should provide transcripts for institutions where:
You earned (or will earn) a degree.
You completed 12 or more credits that do not appear as graded courses on another transcript you are uploading.
Note: If you attended more than 4 schools, only list the 4 most relevant (e.g., your Bachelor’s and Master’s institutions).
Letters of Recommendation
Chemistry, Computer Science, Physics: Two letters of recommendation are required.
Biochemistry and Biophysics, Mathematics, Molecular and Cell Biology, Neuroscience, Psychology: Three letters of recommendation are required.
Academic references (professors, or research/thesis advisors) are strongly preferred. Select a person who can speak to your abilities as a student, research potential, and preparedness for graduate study. You are welcome to submit a professional reference, especially if you do not have a recent academic contact. Select someone who can speak in detail about your skills and approach to work.
Résumé
A current résumé detailing educational and employment history is required. Candidates with little or no full-time work experience should include internships and/or part-time work.
GRE
Submission of GRE scores is optional for most programs (exceptions below). If you choose to submit scores, you may submit unofficial scores at the time of application. If you submitted unofficial scores as part of your application, are offered admission and choose to enroll, you must submit official score reports and send them directly to Brandeis Graduate Admissions from the testing agency.
GRE scores are valid for five (5) years from the original test date. Scores must be valid at the time your application is submitted. The GRE code is 3092.
Computer Science: The GRE is waived for applicants who have earned or will earn a degree from an accredited institution of higher education in the United States prior to enrolling at Brandeis; the GRE is required if you have not earned or will not earn a degree from an accredited institution of higher education in the United States prior to enrolling at Brandeis.
Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, Psychology: Submission of GRE scores is optional.
Biochemistry and Biophysics, Molecular and Cell Biology, Neuroscience: GRE scores are not considered in the admissions process.

School of Social Sciences and Social Policy
Programs: History, Social Policy
Expand All
Application Requirements
Application Fee
The online application fee is $75. This fee is required for all applicants unless you are eligible for an application fee waiver.
Transcripts
You must hold (or be about to earn) a bachelor’s degree from an accredited U.S. or international institution. Three-year international degrees equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's degree are also accepted. Unofficial transcripts are accepted for application review. Official transcripts are only required upon enrollment.
You should provide transcripts for institutions where:
You earned (or will earn) a degree.
You completed 12 or more credits that do not appear as graded courses on another transcript you are uploading.
Note: If you attended more than 4 schools, only list the 4 most relevant (e.g., your Bachelor’s and Master’s institutions).
Letters of Recommendation
History: Two letters of recommendation are required.
Social Policy: Three letters of recommendation are required
Academic references (professors, or research/thesis advisors) are strongly preferred. Select a person who can speak to your abilities as a student, research potential, and preparedness for graduate study. You are welcome to submit a professional reference, especially if you do not have a recent academic contact. Select someone who can speak in detail about your skills and approach to work.
Résumé
A current résumé detailing educational and employment history is required. Candidates with little or no full-time work experience should include internships and/or part-time work.
GRE
GRE scores are not considered for: History
Applicants to the PhD program in Social Policy can choose to either submit GRE scores or submit a Quantitative and Analytical Statement (QAS). The purpose of the QAS is to provide the admissions committee with additional information on your quantitative proficiency.
GRE scores are valid for five (5) years from the original test date. Scores must be valid at the time your application is submitted. The GRE code is 3092.
In the QAS, applicants should detail why they believe they would be successful in a research-based program. Share quantitative classes you have taken, research experience you hold, peer-reviewed research papers you have authored or collaborated on, statistical software you are familiar with and the projects you have utilized statistical software for, etc. Experience with qualitative data analysis and software may be noted but should not be the focus of the statement.
